propositions: Blocking LINK events written before comparability became structural remain durable and unresolved on read, causing incorrect ready/next-batch scheduling and violating parent-first cascade guarantees.

The doctor scan must detect three classes of malformed edges — ancestor-blocking (endpoint is ancestor of other), mis-escalated (resolver returns different pair than recorded), unreadable (endpoint cannot be reduced) — by comparing current resolver output against disk records.

Repair must write replacement links before removing stale ones to ensure an interruption leaves a superset the next run can converge, and must decline repairs creating ambiguous-pair or closed-source violations.
Store-wide scan and repair must not hold outer lock across the write loop to avoid self-deadlock on the non-reentrant tracker write lock, and must refuse to run during active reconciler passes.
Read-only doctor runs must not trigger store reconvergence, while repair runs must initialize the full store state.

Live scan of the rebar repository tracker found 18 blocking edges (9 ancestor-blocking, 9 mis-escalated); repair fixed 12 while 8 residual edges remained inert because their blocked endpoints were closed.
